title: Lark and the Wobbly Pebble
markdown:
Bright sunshine burst through the window and tickled Lark’s nose. Dawn had cracked properly. Birds twittered a chirpy song that made the boots by the door look impatient. She bounced out of bed, red rubber already half on. Outside, Nibbles the otter darted through dewdrops, dark fur sparkling like tiny diamonds. Cool air on her cheeks, damp grass underfoot, the sort of morning that wanted a puzzle.

“Lark! Come quick!” Nibbles chittered, whiskers wiggling. He pointed a wet paw at a tall glass jar on Ms. Rowan’s sun-dappled porch. Inside, a perfectly straight striped pebble looked all bendy, a candy cane left too near a fire.

Rowan tutted, spectacles perched, smile puzzled. “Straight as a ruler this morning. Now a twisted pretzel. Most peculiar.”

Lark poked it through the glass. Still wobbly. She scooped water out with a tiny net. Straight again. Back into the jar — bendy. “The water. It must be doing something.”

Nibbles slapped the porch with his tail. “Tricky water!” He dipped a long dry twig. It looked snapped in half. “Broken!”

Lark giggled. “Not broken. A trick.” She dipped her own finger. Straight, familiar, then curved at the water’s edge. “My finger looks bent too.”

Rowan clasped her hands. “Plain old water?”

Lark dashed to the shed for a small shiny flashlight, pulled a curtain, darkened the porch. “Watch.” The beam shot straight, then — whoosh — as it hit the water and plunged, it bent downward. It did not go straight through.

“The light changed its path!” Nibbles breathed.

“Light likes to travel straight. Air into water — it changes direction. That bending makes the pebble, the finger, the twig look wobbly when they’re straight underneath.” She named it once: refraction.

Nibbles splashed a paw. Lark lifted the pebble out: stripes crisp, perfectly straight. Nibbles nudged a bright blue feather in; it went wavy as a ribbon. “More bending!”

She did not race off after every ripple. She set the pebble on the dry porch boards, where it stayed honest, and left the jar for anyone who still needed convincing. Rowan chuckled. Nibbles shook droplets from his whiskers, which, in air, looked exactly like whiskers.
